I think 4K is being pushed on the public by the television manufactures. It's a rule of thumb that people don't need to buy a new TV more than every ten years, on average. Then we had the HDTV boom, which really earned a lot of money for the TV makers from people replacing their old SDTVs. All businesses need to concern themselves with growth, not just profitability, to stay competitive in a global market, and TV manufacturing is definitely global. So the electronics companies have been trying to find the "next big thing" to push even more constant sales of TVs. (Remember 3D TV's?)

And I don't think the general public wants to pony up the cash already for a new TV. Many of them just got around to getting an HD set, and 1080p is really good enough for most people. (And why do we need 4K? HD already exposes actors' physical flaws, and the bandwidth infrastructure just isn't there yet to support widespread 4K streaming.)
